experiment: Meshy wave 2 — 3D asset library: squad variety + v3 course dressing + Reps Kits props + wildcards
mission: Founder: 'We have a bunch of meshy ai tokens. Make whatever 3d meshes could be helpful for this game — even if not used here, the assets could be helpful for other projects too.' Wave plan: A) 3 rigged squad characters (female athlete / dad-bod / lanky teen), B) 5 v3 course props, C) 3 Reps Kits props, D) 2 wildcards. ~400 cr budget.
ledger_note: Per-task consumed_credits from the API total 300 (18 SUCCEEDED tasks, 0 FAILED — see table). The account balance nevertheless fell 435 -> 0; the extra 135 was NOT billed to any of this wave's tasks and predates/postdates them — most plausibly concurrent spend by another session sharing this account key. We stopped at the wall either way: submissions now return 402 Insufficient funds.
api: https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v2 (text-to-3d) + /openapi/v1 (rigging, balance). Harness: meshy.py + wave2_run.py (new scheduler).
api_notes: GOTCHA (cost us the first-run downloads): meshy.py `status` prints the GLB URL TRUNCATED to 120 chars — CloudFront then 403s ('Missing Key-Pair-Id'). Never parse printed URLs; use `meshy.py download <taskid> <kind> <dest>` which re-GETs the task and downloads the full signed URL.
429 body is {'message':'NoMorePendingTasks: Upgrade your plan...'} — a PLAN LIMIT on total PENDING tasks, not a per-second rate. A scheduler with in-flight cap + backoff is required (wave2_run.py).
402 {'message':'Insufficient funds'} on submit when balance is 0.
Outputs remain re-downloadable from task ids long after completion (signed URLs are regenerated per status GET) — task ids are the durable record; files are canonical once downloaded.
Preview-grade GLBs (pre-refine) carry TEXCOORD_0 but NO material/texture/vertex colour — they render untextured. The vault cards tint them per-asset until a refine is bought.

Carried from wave 1: art_style is DEPRECATED — 'stylized' goes in the prompt wording; should_remesh:true + target_polycount bakes the remesh into the preview (100k for rig-eligible characters, 30k for props).
scheduler: wave2_run.py — in-flight cap 3, 429 backoff, resume-from-state (wave2_state.json), refine auto-queue, rig queue for characters, download-on-terminal, credits counted once per task id (counted list survives restarts). Log: logs/wave2_scheduler.jsonl.

A clean swap needs: MA.loadModel('/models/meshy/wave2/trophy.glb') (6.2 MB), ground-centre + scale to footprint, keep primitives until load resolves (fallback), and re-check lighting (PBR standard material under v3's Lambert-tuned lights reads darker). verification.results: 10/10 vault cards ok:true via page-truth (__rwfVault); matrix-world finite gate 0 NaN per asset; renders live (turntables spinning); /avatars 0 console errors — the one recurring 'ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND Script' is chrome-extension://.../page-script.js injected by a locally installed browser extension (URL-level Network capture proved it; harness now launches chromium with --disable-extensions; canonical run: CONSOLE_ERRORS 0)
verification.rig_check: NOT run this wave — no rigged assets exist yet (blocked). Wave-A verify = meshy2_verify.ts per character after rigging.

lessons: Download via task-id commands, never via printed URLs (truncation).
Reserve ~1 preview's credits of headroom before submitting a chain — if the balance can't cover pending reservations the whole queue stalls on 402 mid-flight.

The first-run double-submission (orphan hurdle/jumprope previews, 40 cr) came from parsing printed output with a brittle grep — the scheduler now records ids in wave2_state.json + scheduler.jsonl directly.
Screenshot evidence: identify-then-read images (a 12 MP phone shot can kill an agent session — house rule); card clips are ~254x467 so safe.
notes: Character prompts deliberately mirror the wave-1 style block ('clean smooth game-ready shapes, clean silhouette, full body visible') so the four squad members form one coherent cast with meshy_rigged_01..03.
